scale.source: Hebrew Wikipedia, "סולמות ארוך וקצר": Israel uses the long scale with the milliard, so ביליון is 10^12; CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50) also writes 1000000000000 as ביליון.

group_mark.source: CLDR main/he.xml inherits the root latn symbols: group ",".

decimal_mark.source: CLDR main/he.xml inherits the root latn symbols: decimal ".".

space_groups.source: CLDR main/he.xml groups digits with ",", not a space.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "3000: <%%thousands< אלפים", the plural takes a count; "אלפים" alone names no number.

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "2000000: שני מיליון", "3000000: <%%spellout-numbering-m< מיליון": מיליון keeps the singular after every count.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "20: עשרים[ >%%and-feminine>]" with "1: ו=%spellout-numbering=": ו joins the last part ("עשרים ושלוש").

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "%%and-feminine" puts ו only before the last part ("מאה ועשרים", "מאה עשרים ושלוש").

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: אלף[ >%%and-feminine>]": ו only before the last part ("אלף ומאה").

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: אלף[ >%%and-feminine>]" with "%%and-feminine: 1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;" and "500: חמש מאות;": ו goes before a unit, not before a hundred.

ordinal_style.source: Lewis Glinert, Modern Hebrew: An Essential Grammar (Routledge), chapter on numerals: ordinal adjectives exist only for 1-10; above ten the cardinal serves.

half_of_scale.source: Lewis Glinert, Modern Hebrew: An Essential Grammar (Routledge), chapter on numerals: "וחצי" after a number adds half of its last unit: "מיליון וחצי" is 1,500,000 and "אלף וחצי" is 1500.

fold_marks.source: Hebrew is written with or without niqqud (vowel points); the points never change which number a word names.

bidi_controls.source: CLDR main/he.xml writes the minus sign as "\u200e-": directional marks stand next to numbers in right-to-left text.

clitic_min_rest.source: The shortest Hebrew number word, "שש", has two letters.

joiner_prefix.source: Lewis Glinert, Modern Hebrew: An Essential Grammar (Routledge), chapter on numerals: the conjunction ו is written joined to the next word ("ושלוש").

clitic_prefix.source: Lewis Glinert, Modern Hebrew: An Essential Grammar (Routledge), chapter on numerals: the article ה and the prepositions ב, ל, מ, כ and the particle ש are written joined to the next word ("השלושה", "בשש").

range_cue.source: Lewis Glinert, Modern Hebrew: An Essential Grammar (Routledge), chapter on numerals: "בין", between; in "בין א ו-ב" the joined ו links the two limits (the other form, "בין א ל-ב", has no joiner).

minus_idioms.source: Hebrew uses no such word in a number.
